**Singapore – the five most recent Deputy Prime Ministers (in chronological order of their first appointment)**  

| # | Deputy Prime Minister | First appointed as DPM | University (under‑graduate degree) |
|---|-----------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1 | **S. Rajaratnam** | 2 May 1985 | **University of Malaya** (Singapore campus) – B.A. (Honours) in History |
| 2 | **Wong Kan Seng** | 25 Jan 1995 | **University of Singapore** (now the National University of Singapore) – B.A. (Honours) in History |
| 3 | **Teo Chee Hean** | 1 Apr 2009 | **University of Cambridge** (Trinity College) – B.Sc. (Honours) in Electrical Engineering |
| 4 | **Heng Swee Keat** | 1 May 2019 | **University of Cambridge** (King’s College) – M.A. in Economics (under‑grad study was a B.A. in Economics) |
| 5 | **Lawrence Wong** | 13 Jun 2022 | **National University of Singapore** – B.Sc. (Honours) in Economics |

*Notes*

* The list follows the order in which each individual first became Deputy Prime Minister, moving forward from the earliest of the five (S. Rajaratnam) to the most recent (Lawrence Wong).  
* Where a Deputy Prime Minister holds multiple degrees, the university listed is the institution that awarded their primary undergraduate (first‑degree) qualification, as this is the usual reference point for “which university did they attend.”  
* All five have also pursued postgraduate studies (e.g., at Harvard Kennedy School, NUS Business School, etc.), but those are not shown here because the question asked specifically for the university they each attended for their main degree.
